column4: Lit 2.5D sea with layered depth, fog, light shafts and teal and amber glows, pixel figures, a dark-fantasy boss arena; the tavern is amber firelight in a stone cellar but no shot of it was taken
The references are inspiration (Dave the Diver, Elden Ring, Dark Souls); there is nothing a screenshot could show about them
Side-on camera that follows the diver, with depth layers sliding at different speeds

Diver mid light-swing with a damage number; roll, guard, flask and heavy swing are in index.html:258 and :387, and the check's keys changed the game. Only the light swing, harpoon and movement were played; the rest was not exercised
Four minion kinds and the elite, each with its own outline and attack, and three bosses drawn; boss arenas in evidence/boss-knight.png, boss-maw.png and boss-leviathan.png
Limp, part drop, flee and rest are written (startLimp, bossCommon) but no fight was played far enough to see one
The check run ended with Bag 1/10 after a harpoon throw, so a fish was caught and kept in the bag
The counter, cauldron, shrine, anvil and hearth menus are written; only the dive door menu was exercised, by the check run
Depth scaling in mkMob, the new minion per depth and phases per boss are written but never compared across depths in play
The YOU DIED screen showed in evidence/boss-leviathan.png, but picking the lost souls back up was never played
Sell, cook and sharpen are written, never exercised
Harpoon catch reached the bag in the check run; killing and reeling in minions for items is in index.html:339
The shrine levels and the anvil blade levels are written, never exercised
Same as F3
The check run started at the hearth, walked right to the door, opened the dive menu and went down to depth 1
The first dive has no boss silhouette gliding across the dark; the boss only appears at the arena gate
A red elite angler with a double lunge sits past x=1450 in depth 1 (index.html:222) and shows in the shot
Minion stats rise per depth in code, never compared in play
Death drops souls and catch in code, and the death screen showed; the second-death loss was never played
Difficulty can only be judged by a person playing
